source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: Unergative verbal roots and unergative verbs as √-suffix combinations
notes: In (60) the diminutive verb occurs with a regular non-diminutive noun. Again, as in (59) the verbal diminutive can qualify the running event itself as a series of quick happenings or it can qualify the accusative direct object as having a small size.
en: a) Misha ran over a small field. b) Misha ran around a field in short bouts.
